questions.text: Under PD 1096 RIRR Section 1211, what is the minimum wall thickness for a residential chimney made of solid masonry?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 100 mm solid masonry. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1211.

questions.text: For a chimney serving a medium-heat appliance, what lining rule does Section 1211 state?

options.text: A 100 mm firebrick lining beginning 600 mm below the chimney connector entrance
A 25 mm metal lining above the roof only
No lining if the chimney is under 7.50 m high
A wood liner protected by sheet metal

questions.rationale: Correct answer: A 100 mm firebrick lining beginning 600 mm below the chimney connector entrance. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1211.
questions.explanation: Fire clay lining = standard; Firebrick alternative = 500 mm minimum. The 500 mm thickness is counterintuitively large — it reflects the fact that firebrick requires much greater mass to achieve equivalent thermal protection to purpose-made fire clay liner tiles.

questions.text: What minimum height rule applies to a chimney above the roof under Section 1211?

options.text: 600 mm above the roof and 600 mm above the highest part within 3.00 m

questions.rationale: Correct answer: 600 mm above the roof and 600 mm above the highest part within 3.00 m. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1211.
questions.explanation: 600 mm above roof + 600 mm above any building part within 3.00 m. Both thresholds are the same (600 mm) but apply to different reference points. The 3.00 m horizontal distance is the radius within which nearby building parts must be considered.

questions.text: What clearance from combustible material applies to a chimney located within a building or structure?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 50 mm. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1211.
questions.explanation: Interior clearance = 50 mm; Exterior clearance = 25 mm. The interior requires more clearance because heat transfer to concelead combustible framing is harder to detect and more dangerous. The 150 mm figure belongs to fireplace opening clearances, not framing clearances.

questions.text: What minimum projection in front of the fireplace opening is required for the reinforced concrete hearth slab?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 450 mm. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1211.
questions.explanation: 200 mm below the lowest inlet — not at the inlet, not 100 mm, not 300 mm. The lining must extend beyond the inlet zone to protect the masonry at the highest-temperature point of the flue system.

questions.text: What minimum firebox depth is stated for fireplaces under Section 1211?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 500 mm. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1211.
questions.explanation: Outer wall: 200 mm standard, 150 mm with firebrick inner face. Firebox wall: 250 mm standard, 200 mm with firebrick. Hearth: ≥100 mm thick. These four distinct wall thickness values are each independently testable.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 RIRR Section 1211, what is the minimum wall thickness for a residential chimney made of solid masonry?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 100 mm solid masonry. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1211.
questions.explanation: Hearth: 450 mm front, 300 mm sides, 100 mm thick. Three separate hearth dimensions. The asymmetry (450 front vs 300 sides) reflects that embers are more likely to roll forward than sideways when falling from a fireplace opening.

questions.text: For a chimney serving a medium-heat appliance, what lining rule does Section 1211 state?

options.text: A 100 mm firebrick lining beginning 600 mm below the chimney connector entrance
A 25 mm metal lining above the roof only
No lining if the chimney is under 7.50 m high
A wood liner protected by sheet metal

questions.rationale: Correct answer: A 100 mm firebrick lining beginning 600 mm below the chimney connector entrance. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1211.
questions.explanation: Damper specs: No. 12 gauge + 90% of flue area when open. Both figures are precise and independently testable. The 90% requirement prevents damper installation that would unduly restrict draft even when fully retracted.

questions.text: What minimum height rule applies to a chimney above the roof under Section 1211?

options.text: 600 mm above the roof and 600 mm above the highest part within 3.00 m

questions.rationale: Correct answer: 600 mm above the roof and 600 mm above the highest part within 3.00 m. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1211.
questions.explanation: PH = 20 mm max; US (NFPA 211) = 12.7 mm max. Philippine standard is more permissive. This is a classic comparison question: Philippine vs international standard. The direction of difference (PH allows larger) is the testable fact.

questions.text: What clearance from combustible material applies to a chimney located within a building or structure?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 50 mm. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1211.
questions.explanation: Small incinerator: ≤110 kg/hr AND ≤0.50 sq.m grate — BOTH criteria required. 95 kg/hr passes; 0.45 sq.m passes → small. Medium-heat chimney ≤7.50 m → lining to top. This question tests dual-criteria classification plus the associated chimney rule.

questions.text: What minimum projection in front of the fireplace opening is required for the reinforced concrete hearth slab?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 450 mm. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1211.
questions.explanation: Three corbeling rules: 150 mm total maximum, 300 mm minimum wall, 25 mm per course maximum. All three apply simultaneously. Corbeling redirects chimney location horizontally while maintaining structural integrity — excessive corbeling creates instability and cracking.
